I5.quote: Porous materials such as metal organic frameworks (MOFs), zeolite templated carbons (ZTC), and some porous polymers have endeared the research community for their attractiveness for hydrogen (H2) storage applications.

notes: Original research article (Frontiers in Chemistry, 'ORIGINAL RESEARCH'); is_retracted false and no retraction statement in the text; no statement that all H2 values were published before (Table 2 literature rows are labelled with references, the rows marked 'This work' are the paper's own). H2 uptake was measured at 77 K up to 1 bar on a Micromeritics ASAP 2020 HD analyser (a static volumetric gas-sorption instrument); the paper does not itself use the word 'volumetric'. Carbon sorbent measured: pristine ZTC (zeolite templated carbon, carbonised at 900 C), 2.38 wt% H2 and BET 3,206 m2/g; the PIM-1/80 wt% ZTC composite (80 wt% ZTC) is also reported (1.87 wt%, BET 2,433 m2/g). Non-carbon samples (UiO-66(Zr), PIM-1/UiO-66 composite) are also measured.
